newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-MONTPELLIER AND BORDEAUX CLASH AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MONTPELLIER AND BORDEAUX CLASH AGAIN.

text.p: Montpellier host Bordeaux on Saturday for what has become a regular of the French soccer season, the two southern sides having met three times already.
Bordeaux lead 2-1 after their league win at home early in the season and their League Cup semifinal victory in February.
But Bordeaux will be seeking revenge after having lost the last encounter between the two, 2-1 at home in a French Cup quarter-final last week.
This fourth clash is all the more intriguing as apart from the defeats they have inflicted on each other, neither Montpellier and Bordeaux has lost a match since the beginning of the year.
Only Nantes, who have won or drawn their last 24 matches, have done better.

"Everybody talks about Nantes but in our last 24 matches before our Cup quarter-final against Montpellier we only had lost away in Bastia and Auxerre. It is not bad, is it?" Bordeaux coach Rolland Courbis said.

Courbis was speaking on Friday just before appearing in a Toulon court where he was sentenced to six months jail for tax evasion. But Courbis will still be at Saturday's match after being released on bail pending an appeal.
Courbis said he hoped his team will have recovered from last week's defeat.
"If we play the same as in the second half last Saturday, anybody can beat us. Now the players have a professional duty to overcome this loss," he said.
"If I had the choice, I would rather we had won last week's match than this one," he added.
Sixth-placed Bordeaux need points to remain in contention for a place in Europe next season although they have another route when they meet Strasbourg in the League Cup final on April 12.
Bordeaux will be without former European footballer of the year Jean-Pierre Papin who has taken his daughter, who is ill, to the U.S. for medical treatment.
Papin will probably be replaced by Kaba Diawara.
